verdicts.reason: The packet carries four vocatives (vr̥trahantama, úgra, praṇetar, vaso VOC) plus the 2SG imperative gahi, and the translation opens with the anchored vocative "Chief Vrtra-slayer", so address force and an addressee referent are both directly evidenced.

gahi is an imperative (IMP AOR 2SG) and the translation reads "think of all, All that concerneth us", with naḥ (GEN PL) grounding the speaking group as beneficiary; both anchored spans appear verbatim and the single appositional outcome is correctly left unsplit under Rule 3.

vr̥trahántama- is tagged degree SUP in the packet and renders as "Chief Vrtra-slayer", so foremost rank as Vrtra-slayer is an entity-level quality attributed to the addressee, distinct in relation force from the INVOKES address on the same wording.

The anchored "Excellent" is in the translation and corresponds to vaso (vásu- VOC M SG), a vocative epithet of the addressee rather than of the requested outcome, so the quality and its binding are both directly evidenced.
"Mighty Guide" is anchored verbatim and matches the vocatives úgra and praṇetar in pada c, supporting both the "leading role" and "might" qualifiers as attributed properties of the same addressee.

The instrumental means is well evidenced (dhiyā́ INS F SG, translated "through the hymn of Visvamanas"), but whether that named dhī́- ("thought/vision/prayer") counts as a RITUAL_EVENT rather than an EXPRESSES concept or a plain ASSOCIATED_WITH is genuinely arguable, and the RELATION anchor is only the bare preposition "through".

viśvámanasaḥ is GEN M SG attached to the hymn and the translation reads "the hymn of Visvamanas", with the packet's traditional_rishi_labels "vaiyaśvo viśvamanāḥ" corroborating a person-like referent, correctly routed to ONTOLOGY_GAP_REF / PERSON_LIKE_REFERENT_UNMODELED with no more specific allowed predicate available.

The translation states "The foolish brought the ne'er-bewildered forward", giving a narrated (not commanded) action with both roles the object assigns, and Sanskrit mūrā́ḥ (NOM PL) / ámūram (ACC SG) match agent and patient.

"great" stands in the translation's appositive epithet list attached to "the ne'er-bewildered"; the packet morphology for mahā́m is GEN PL rather than agreeing ACC SG, but Rule on explicitness permits resting the binding on the supplied translation.
"Victor" is in the translation's epithet list for the ne'er-bewildered and is carried by jáyantam (√ji-, ACC SG PTCP) agreeing with ámūram, an entity-level quality distinct from any action.
"Song-inspirer" is in the translation and corresponds to vipodhā́m (ACC SG) agreeing with ámūram, so both the descriptive force and the described referent are packet-supported.
"Fort-destroyer" is in the translation and corresponds to purā́m darmā́ṇam (GEN PL + ACC SG) in pada b, an independently anchored epithet rather than a restatement of the other three.

"Leading the Youth gold-bearded" is a narrated participial action in the translation, matching náyantaḥ (NOM PL PTCP) with gárbham (ACC SG) as patient, and is a different action from the "brought forward" of the first assertion.

"gold-bearded" (híriśmaśrum, ACC SG) is an entity-level quality of the Youth stated independently of the leading action, so Rule 4 permits it alongside the DESCRIBES_ACTION rather than making it a duplicate.

The translation's final clause "they turned their hymn to profit" narrates the action, with dhíyam (ACC SG) as the patient and dhuḥ (3PL AOR INJ) as the verb; the "to profit" qualifier is kept in its own field rather than folded into an identity.

The named inference step is factually accurate about the packet (mūrá- 1 and its a-privative ámūra- do sit adjacent in pada b, mirrored by "The foolish" / "ne'er-bewildered"), so this stays within the one step STRONG_INFERENCE allows, but whether that juxtaposition asserts a contrast or is merely the agent-patient pairing already captured by the "brought forward" assertion is genuinely arguable, and the RELATION anchor "The foolish" covers only one pole of the claimed opposition.
Token PA:T003 'agne' is VOC SG and the translation reads 'Ours art thou, wondrous Agni', so second-person address of the supplied key VG:DEVATA:AGNIH is direct.

'Ours art thou' plus token PA:T002 'naḥ' (DAT PL) directly attributes an entity-level relation of belonging to the addressed Agni, and the qualifier 'by wisdom and bounteousness of power' is quoted verbatim from the same clause.
Token PA:T004 'adbhuta' (VOC, agreeing with 'agne') and the translation 'wondrous Agni' give an entity-level quality attributed to Agni, distinct from the belonging claim in the previous assertion.

'The might of Asuras rests on thee' is narrated, not wished for (PC:T011 'aruhat' AOR IND ACT, with 'asuryàm' NOM and 'tvé' LOC), so Rule 5 is satisfied and both participant heads restate wording present in the packet.

The comparison particle PD:T014 'ná' with PD:T013 'mitráḥ' ('like Mitra') explicitly links the passage to the supplied key VG:DEVATA:MITRAH and no narrower allowed predicate encodes a simile, though the assertion carries no TARGET anchor on the word 'Mitra'.

The supplied translation attaches the epithet to Mitra in 'like Mitra worshipful in act' (PD:T015 'yajñíyaḥ' with PD:T012 'krāṇā́'), so the quality is directly attributed to the anchored entity, even though the simile leaves open whether the epithet also characterises the compared Agni.

The packet's "So may Sarasvati auspicious send good luck" plus the subjunctive kr̥ṇavat (SBJV, 3SG) is exactly the "may X occur" / sending-and-bestowing request force of Rule 2, and the OUTCOME anchor "send good luck" is the concise desired result rather than a copied sentence.

"When praised in Jamadagni's way and lauded as Vasistha lauds" carries praise force, and the middle participles gr̥ṇānā́ / stuvānā́ are NOM.F.SG agreeing with sárasvatī, so the supplied Sarasvatī key is the correct praised referent and both qualifiers are verbatim packet wording.

bhadrā́ (NOM.F.SG, token T003, rendered "auspicious" adjacent to "Sarasvati" in the translation) is an entity-level quality attributed to Sarasvatī and is distinct from the ACC.N.SG bhadrám that grounds the REQUESTS outcome, so it is not a duplicate of assertion 1.

"lauded as Vasistha lauds" (vasiṣṭhavát, token T013) names a second person-like referent for which the packet supplies only a rishi label and no bindable key, so the same ontology-gap treatment holds and it is an object distinct from assertion 6.

"waxing in their strength" renders śvātrā́saḥ (NOM PL, pada c), a distinct quality from the other epithets and independently anchored, so Rule 1 emission is appropriate.
"for ever stirring" corresponds to bhuraṇyávaḥ (NOM PL, pada c) and is a separate epithet from śvātrā́saḥ, not a restatement of the strength assertion.

bráhma (ACC) with jinvatam (IMP.2.DU) and the translation "Give spirit to our prayer" give an imperative request force with a directly anchored desired outcome.
the second jinvatam with dhíyaḥ (ACC.PL), coordinated by utá and rendered "and animate our thoughts", is an independently coordinated outcome, so the Rule 3 split from the bráhma request is correct.

sunvatáḥ is the PRS.PTCP of √su- governing sómam, so the pressing act is lexically present in the packet and the declared STRONG_INFERENCE is the single permitted step of naming that pressing as the ritual event.

jinvatam (2 DU IMP, T002) with dhenū́ḥ (ACC F PL, T001) is imperative request force under Rule 2, and the OUTCOME anchor "strength unto the milch-kine" is exact translation wording with the beneficiary correctly kept as a qualifier rather than a separate outcome.

hatám (2 DU IMP, T006) with rákṣāṃsi (ACC N PL, T007) is an independent imperative rendered "slay ye the Raksasas", and the outcome head "slay the Raksasas" is the desired resulting action rather than a bare grammatical object.

sédhatam (2 DU IMP, T008) with ámīvāḥ (ACC F PL, T009) is a distinct imperative from hatám, so "drive away disease" stands as its own coordinated outcome under Rule 3 with both anchors on exact translation wording.

sómam (ACC M SG, T014) qualified by sunvatáḥ (GEN SG PRS PTCP, T015) plus the vocative aśvinā gives the addressee, and although pada d has no finite verb token the supplied translation states "the presser's Soma, Asvins drink", which the explicitness policy allows to carry the relation as EXPLICIT.

sajóṣasau is NOM M DU (T010) and so predicates the state of concord of the dual Asvins, with uṣásā (INS, T011) and sū́ryeṇa (INS, T012) supplying the two comitative qualifiers; this is an entity-level state, not an action, so Rule 4 places it in DESCRIBES rather than DESCRIBES_ACTION.

The anchor "presser's" is exactly sunvatáḥ, a present active participle of √su- (T015), so the pressing is an ongoing action of a human agent that is presupposed rather than commanded, keeping it outside Rule 5's exclusion, and the recorded inference step is the single named step STRONG_INFERENCE permits.

sómam (ACC M SG, T014) is a physical material explicitly present with the supplied lexical mention VG:DEVATA:SOMAH, and the qualifiers "pressed" / "in the presser's possession" are carried by the genitive participle sunvatáḥ, so under Rule 6 the substance role is a distinct typed role rather than a duplicate of the REQUESTS outcome, though the assertion anchors only "drink" and never the substance wording itself.

"may this be health and force to us" is clearly request force with "health" (śám, T006) as an evidenced outcome, but the pair sits in a single copular clause with one subject "this", so a reasonable reader could take "health and force" as one composite desired state rather than two.

Same clause as the preceding assertion: "force" (yós, T007) is directly evidenced as a wished-for state, but whether the coordinated "health and force" complement is one outcome or two is exactly the split-or-merge call Rule 3 leaves arguable here.

"May we obtain firm ground" matches the optative aśīmáhi (OPT AOR 1PL, T012) governing the accusative gādhám (T013), giving request force and an independently standing outcome with a first-person beneficiary the wording grounds.

"room for resting" renders the second accusative pratiṣṭhā́m (T015) explicitly coordinated by utá (T014) under the same optative, so it stands as a separately desired result rather than a modifier of "firm ground".

"incessantly invokes you for your favour" (johaviti, vam ACC DU, avase) carries invocation force onto a dual addressee and the qualifiers "invoked incessantly" and "invoked for favour" track that same wording; leaving the referent OPAQUE is defensible because no lexical-mention key names indravaruna in this packet.

"hear ye mine invocation" is a 2DU imperative (srnutam) addressed to the pair, so Rule 2 request force holds, and the head "hear my invocation" is the desired resulting action rather than a copied sentence, with RELATION and OUTCOME anchors on the exact wording.

"This man, most diligent, seeking after riches" (ayam NOM SG M, purutamah SUP, rayiyan PTCP) attributes entity-level qualities to a person-like referent that no supplied key resolves, matching the PERSON_LIKE_REFERENT_UNMODELED gap case, and the anchor "most diligent" carries that attribution.
